proofCandidates.fullText:
Modal Clusters GA: Serverless Multi-Node GPUs for Every Enterprise

Modal has announced the general availability of Modal Clusters [1], delivering on-demand, multi-node GPU compute with up to 6.4 Tbps InfiniBand RDMA behind a single `@modal.clustered` decorator [1][1]. The launch directly targets the infrastructure complexity that has historically confined petaFLOP-scale AI training and inference to the largest cloud-native organizations. With the AI Platforms market on a base-case trajectory of $181.3B in 2026 and $496.9B by 2030 at a 28.7% CAGR [2], Modal's serverless cluster primitive arrives as enterprises accelerate from AI experimentation to production-grade, multi-node workloads. What is Covered in this Article Modal Clusters GA: single-decorator multi-node GPU access [1] [1]

InfiniBand RDMA at up to 6.4 Tbps with gVisor open-source integration [1] [1]

Production customer deployments at frontier scale [1] [1] [1]

Enterprise AI infrastructure adoption barriers [3] [3]

AI Platforms market growth context [2] The News: Modal announced the general availability of Modal Clusters [1] after 1.5 years of battle-testing [1]. Developers access multi-node GPU compute through a single `@modal.clustered` decorator with an optional `rdma=True` flag [1]. Clusters communicate via InfiniBand verbs at up to 6.4 Tbps, automatically configured for PyTorch and NCCL [1]. Billing is by the second with no hourly reservations required, and code runs on a cluster within seconds of requesting it [1]. Modal built a new gang scheduler using an observe-plan-act loop that schedules N nodes atomically, grouping by availability zone and network ID [1]. RDMA support was built into gVisor and upstreamed to the open-source project [1]. Modal Clusters GA: Serverless Multi-Node GPUs for Every Enterprise Analyst Take: Modal Clusters GA represents a meaningful architectural shift in how enterprises access large-scale GPU compute. By collapsing weeks of multi-node infrastructure setup into a single decorator, Modal removes the operational barrier that has historically made petaFLOP-scale training and inference the exclusive domain of hyperscalers and well-resourced AI labs. The timing aligns with a market inflection point: the AI Platforms market is forecast at $181.3B in 2026, growing to $496.9B by 2030 at a 28.7% CAGR, on a base-case trajectory [2]. Systems Innovation Behind the Simplicity The single-decorator abstraction conceals substantial engineering depth. Modal's new gang scheduler uses an observe-plan-act loop to schedule N nodes atomically, grouping by availability zone and network ID [1], solving the fundamental problem that a per-node greedy scheduler cannot handle multi-node placement correctly. The RDMA implementation is equally notable: Modal automated RDMA setup across multiple clouds and built RDMA support into gVisor, upstreaming those changes to the open-source project [1]. This matters because RDMA has historically required cloud-specific drivers, environment variables, and userspace libraries, creating a per-cloud integration burden that most teams cannot absorb. The performance delta is concrete: every training step of GLM 4.7 syncs approximately 717 GB of BF16 weights, taking nearly two minutes over 50 Gbps TCP but under two seconds over RDMA [1]. For inference, prefill-decode disaggregation on Llama 3.1 70B moves roughly 10 GB of KV cache per 32k-token prompt within a time-to-first-token budget of a few hundred milliseconds [1], a constraint that only RDMA can reliably satisfy at scale. Production Validation Across Frontier Workloads Three customer deployments demonstrate that Modal Clusters handles frontier workloads in production, not just controlled benchmarks. Decagon used Modal Clusters to fine-tune open models with up to a trillion parameters using the Miles framework for customer experience AI agents [1], with Cyrus Asgari, Research Lead at Decagon, noting that trillion-parameter fine-tuning is a substantial infrastructure challenge that Modal Clusters resolved. 1x pre-trains its NEO home robot world model on Modal Clusters using multi-node B300 clusters with RDMA, scaling to hundreds of GPUs on demand [1]. Runway's Gen-4.5 and Aleph 2.0 frontier video generation models use Modal Clusters for multi-node inference, with Modal's autoscaler scaling clusters as a unit across a global compute pool [1]. Collectively, these deployments span training, fine-tuning, and inference, validating the primitive across the full AI development lifecycle. Addressing the Enterprise Infrastructure Gap Modal's launch maps directly onto documented enterprise pain points. Among AI decision makers, 55.4% cite AI agent reliability and hallucination management in production as a top adoption challenge [3], a barrier that Modal's automated GPU health assurance and RDMA remediation is designed to reduce for infrastructure-related reliability failures. Separately, 41.8% of enterprise AI decision makers monitor time-to-first-token as a critical inference metric [3], and Modal's RDMA-enabled KV cache transfer reduces that latency from minutes to seconds [1][1]. The competitive positioning is also relevant: enterprises that deploy AI on provider-managed cloud platforms such as AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Azure [3] represent a large installed base for which Modal's cloud-agnostic, multi-cloud RDMA automation offers a differentiated alternative to single-cloud cluster offerings. Meanwhile, 51.0% of enterprises pursue a balanced mix of in-house and vendor solutions [3], aligning with Modal's model of abstracting infrastructure complexity while preserving full programmatic control for developers. Market Timing and Competitive Implications The AI Platforms market's base-case trajectory of $181.3B in 2026 growing to $496.9B by 2030 at a 28.7% CAGR [2] reflects an industry moving from proof-of-concept to production at scale. Modal's serverless cluster primitive arrives precisely as enterprises face the infrastructure step-change from single-node experimentation to multi-node production workloads. The per-second billing model with no hourly reservations required [1] removes a common friction point for organizations evaluating multi-node compute, opening a segment of the market that traditional cloud cluster offerings do not serve efficiently. The open-source contribution of gVisor RDMA support [1] also signals a platform strategy: by expanding the ecosystem, Modal builds developer familiarity and reduces switching friction over time. Decagon Unveils AI for the Era of Personal Agents at Dialogues Published at October 1st 2026, 1:30 PM EDT via Business Wire ⓘ This article is third-party content and does not represent the views of this site. We make no guarantees regarding its accuracy or completeness. New products for the next frontier headline the company's second annual flagship conference, plus new partnerships and industry-leading speakers Decagon, the leader in conversational AI agents for concierge customer experiences, today hosts its second annual flagship conference, Decagon Dialogues, ushering in an era of AI that meets customers — and their agents — however they choose to engage. With Voice 3, Personal Agent Gateway, Agent Modules, and Duet Apprentice, Decagon is meeting the moment where customers expect to be treated like someone the business already knows, not a ticket number in a queue. Frontier AI models are intelligent about the world in general, but a model that knows the world is not the same as one that knows a specific business: its policies, its systems, its customers, and the knowledge that used to live in one person's head. Closing that gap is what Decagon spent the last year building toward, and today's product launches are the result. Frontier models keep improving, but still don’t account for the nuances of how an agent should sound on the phone, how it should interact with a customer versus that customer’s personal agent, how a bank conducts a fraud dispute versus how an airline rebooks a stranded passenger, or how a company onboards and trains its best teammates. Each product announced today delivers that expertise: Voice 3 knows customer experience , combining a new duplex architecture with Chord, the first voice model from Decagon Labs, for more natural customer conversations. Most voice agents combine general-purpose speech models with cascaded pipelines that struggle to coordinate conversation with ongoing work. Customers hear the result in stiff delivery and awkward pauses or interruptions. The Chord voice model is built for the intonation and natural pauses of a live call, slowing down for details like confirmation codes, then returning to a conversational pace. Voice 3 also introduces a new duplex architecture where conversation and task execution run in parallel, letting the voice agent narrate its progress and answer follow-up questions during a long-running task, rather than putting the customer on hold.

Enterprises first deployed Decagon’s agents to resolve support tickets, and the company said those agents now qualify leads, onboard customers, collect payments, and grow relationships. The new releases are organized around what Decagon calls an AI concierge that meets customers however they choose to engage, including when a customer sends a personal AI agent to get something done on their behalf. Voice 3 and the Chord Speech Model Voice 3 ships with Chord, the first voice model from Decagon Labs, post-trained specifically for customer conversations. Decagon said the model shapes speech phrase by phrase, slowing down for details like phone numbers and confirmation codes before returning to a conversational pace. Existing brand-customization controls carry over, including voice selection, pronunciation of business-specific terms, and delivery tuning. Voice 3 also runs on a new duplex architecture with two layers operating in parallel: a low-latency conversational model handles listening and speaking, while a more powerful model manages reasoning, tool calling, and guardrail enforcement behind the conversation. The agent processes incoming audio even while speaking, so it talks through a casual “mhm” but yields on a genuine interruption, and it can narrate progress and answer follow-up questions during a long-running task rather than putting the caller on hold. Decagon reported that in a blind test across three pairs of recordings, each pairing a real person with the same voice run through Chord, on average approximately 90% of listeners could not identify the human. The company said Chord is trained on licensed data and consented voice talent, never on customer-owned data. Voice 3 supports more than 70 languages, detects the caller’s language, and switches automatically even when callers move between languages mid-sentence, according to the company, which said every language is validated by native speakers before it ships. Christian Niedworok, Lead of Digital Service Communication at Deutsche Telekom, said in the Voice 3 announcement that “the voice sounds like it’s actually listening, and it keeps the conversation moving instead of going quiet while it works.” Personal Agent Gateway and the PACT Protocol In the Personal Agent Gateway announcement, Decagon noted that in the month leading up to the event, Meta launched Muse, OpenAI introduced dots, and Instinct started placing phone calls for users. The company described these as personal agents that book, buy, cancel, and negotiate on their owners’ behalf, and said they are already contacting customer support. The gateway combines two capabilities. Personal agent detection flags likely personal agents across chat and voice using signals from the business and the platform, with each business deciding what happens next and what those agents can access. A dedicated personal agent channel sits alongside chat, email, and voice with separate Agent Operating Procedures (AOPs), so the same request can follow a different workflow depending on whether a person or an agent is asking. Permissions live inside the AOPs: businesses define the scopes an agent can request and mark which sections require each one, and those sections are never exposed to an agent lacking the required scope. Decagon described an airline example in which a traveler’s personal agent requests permission to view and rebook flights but the traveler approves only viewing; the airline’s agent shares earlier flight options but cannot make the change until the traveler authorizes rebooking. Decagon also introduced PACT, short for Personal Agent Consent & Trust, a protocol it said lets a person’s agent act on their behalf under permissions the service defines and the person grants. PACT builds on the Agent2Agent protocol, which covers how agents find each other and exchange messages, and adds delegated authorization built on OAuth 2.0 so an agent can prove which person it represents and what that person allowed it to do. The specification is available, and Decagon said it is working with personal agent providers and enterprise customers to shape it. Agent Modules and Duet Apprentice Agent Modules combine infrastructure, analytics, and campaign orchestration for customer journeys beyond support, including lead qualification, onboarding, and collections, across financial services, travel and hospitality, healthcare, retail, and telecom. The customer’s team defines the business logic while Duet draws on the company’s SOPs, policies, integrations, and knowledge sources to translate processes into agent behavior. In collections, for example, teams set disclosure language, approved payment plan tiers, and conditions that require a handoff to a human. Before launch, Simulations test agent behavior against personas with varying intents, such as a customer disputing a balance; once live, module-specific analytics track journey outcomes such as recovered payments, not just whether a conversation was resolved. Campaign Composer sequences touchpoints across channels and time, from an SMS payment reminder to a follow-up call and, when needed, a handoff to a collections representative, with each step beginning from prior interaction history. A shared management layer supports multiple instances with separate access controls per team while analytics aggregate across instances, and memory carries across sessions, channels, and instances, according to the Agent Modules announcement. Duet Apprentice is in beta, with general availability planned. Decagon said Duet arrived earlier in 2026 as an agent-building partner and that it writes more than 70% of the AOPs running on the platform. With Apprentice, Duet reads onboarding documents and process wikis in Notion, Confluence, SharePoint, or Google Drive without migration, and learns from escalated conversations handled by experienced representatives. Plugins for Slack and Microsoft Teams let Duet follow discussions as policies change, draft AOP updates when tagged, and ask for clarity in the same channel when a thread is ambiguous. Decagon stated that what Duet learns belongs to the customer, stays in the customer’s workspace, and is not used to train models outside it. Anne Young, Senior Manager, AI & Process Automation at Questrade, said in the Duet Apprentice announcement, “With Duet, we confidently launch new features on a weekly basis.” Jenn Palk-Cogley, Head of CX and User Operations at Perplexity, said Duet lets her team build and iterate on agent logic without pulling resources away from the roadmap.

proofCandidates.title: Decagon Introduces Voice 3 Agent With Chord Speech Model
proofCandidates.summary: Decagon introduced Voice 3, a voice AI agent, and Chord, its first speech model, at Decagon Dialogues 2026. The agent supports over 70 languages and uses a duplex architecture, with evaluation showing resolution rate increases and a blind test where 45.7% of listeners thought the AI voice was human.
proofCandidates.fullText:
Decagon introduced Voice 3, its voice AI agent for customer calls, and Chord, the first speech model from Decagon Labs, at the company’s Decagon Dialogues 2026 event on October 1, 2026, saying the agent supports more than 70 languages and runs on a new duplex architecture. In the Voice 3 announcement, authored by Product Manager Quique Lores and Senior Product Marketing Manager Ariana Xiang, Decagon described Voice 3 as its most advanced voice AI agent yet. The agent speaks through Chord, and it launched alongside three other products at Decagon Dialogues 2026. In the Decagon Dialogues 2026 post, co-founders Jesse Zhang, Decagon’s chief executive, and Ashwin Sreenivas, its president, named the other three releases: Personal Agent Gateway, which identifies customers’ personal AI agents and gives them a dedicated channel to engage with a business; Agent Modules, which extend an agent across journeys beyond support; and Duet Apprentice, which lets the company’s Duet system learn a business from internal resources and escalated customer conversations. Enterprises first put Decagon agents to work resolving support tickets, the co-founders wrote, and those agents now qualify leads, onboard customers, collect payments, and grow relationships. The four releases expand how customers reach what Decagon calls an AI concierge and what it can do for them. Voice 3 and the Chord Speech Model Chord is the first voice model trained by Decagon Labs, and the company says it was post-trained on real-world customer experience conversations rather than for the broad range of uses most voice models serve, from audiobook narration to video-game voiceovers. Decagon says the model shapes speech phrase by phrase, slowing down for a confirmation code or phone number and then returning to a conversational pace, instead of relying on one global speed setting. Existing voice customization controls carry over: voice selection, pronunciation of business-specific terms, and delivery tuned to the business. Voice 3 supports more than 70 languages without requiring teams to build a separate agent for each one, according to the announcement. It detects the caller’s language and switches automatically, even when a caller moves between languages mid-sentence, and Decagon says its locale-specific voices reflect how people speak in each market and are validated by native speakers before they ship. Decagon states that Chord is trained on licensed data and consented voice talent, never on customer-owned data. Christian Niedworok, Lead of Digital Service Communication at Deutsche Telekom, said in the announcement that years of IVR systems have trained customers to speak in short fragments just to reach a human, and that Decagon’s voice sounds like it is actually listening and keeps the conversation moving instead of going quiet while it works. Chime Chief Operating Officer Janelle Sallenave said Decagon Voice lets Chime combine high performance and seamless brand customization with cross-channel memory, keeping every interaction connected and true to its member-first values. Training Pipeline and Base Model A companion post by Samuel Zhang, a member of Decagon’s technical staff focused on agent orchestration, describes how Chord was built. Its training pipeline is designed to preserve the texture of real conversation, including shifting pace, natural emphasis, pauses, and filler words, rather than scrubbing recordings into the clean, even read the post says makes voices sound synthetic. Two methods support that approach: a verbatim transcription process that preserves pacing, emphasis, and disfluencies, and a recording method that combines the content of a script with the naturalness of free-flowing conversation rather than a performative read from voice actors. For the base model, Decagon post-trained a tokenizer-free diffusion model. The post argues that discretizing audio into tokens discards information at every tokenization step, while a token-free representation stays close to lossless and preserves the fine detail that separates a voice that is merely intelligible from one that sounds present. It also makes the model far more steerable, the post says, allowing Decagon to shape emotion, pace, and emphasis with precision. In production, Chord is served on Modal. Duplex Architecture Decagon says most voice agents run a cascaded pipeline in which speech-to-text transcribes the caller, a large language model decides how to respond, and text-to-speech speaks the reply, with each stage adding delay and the coordination between stages making natural turn-taking difficult. Voice 3 replaces that arrangement with a duplex architecture that runs two layers in parallel: a low-latency conversational model handles listening and speaking, from answers to progress updates, while a more powerful model manages reasoning, tool calling, and guardrail enforcement behind the conversation. According to the company, the agent processes incoming audio even while it is speaking, so it talks through a caller saying “mhm” but yields on a genuine interruption. It narrates its progress during long lookups, answers follow-up questions while a task is still running, and helps with smaller requests in between, rather than leaving the caller in silence or on hold. Company-Reported Evaluation Results Zhang’s post reports on customers in telecom, financial services, and travel and hospitality that switched from an off-the-shelf voice to a voice on Chord, comparing the same programs before and after with only the voice changed. Resolution rate increased in every case, Decagon reports: up 6.1 points for the telecom customer, 7.1 points for the financial services provider, and 2.6 points for the travel brand. Barge rates, which Decagon defines as the share of calls where the caller’s only goal is to reach a human, decreased by 14.5, 6.1, and 5.3 points across the three customers. In a blind listening test across three voices, listeners heard the same audio samples spoken once by Chord and once by the voice talent it was modeled on, and were asked to pick which was the AI. Decagon reports that 45.7% of listeners believed the real human voice was the AI, a result the company describes as close enough to a 50-50 coin flip that the two were effectively indistinguishable. The Voice 3 announcement summarizes the result as approximately 90% of users unable to tell. Decagon also reports a preference test that put Chord head-to-head against three other speech models it describes as leading, with the same words spoken by each and listeners asked to choose the voice they would most want to talk to as a customer with a problem. Across 185 listeners, the company says Chord placed first overall at 36.2% and reached as high as 48.4% in individual rounds. Looking ahead, Decagon says the harder and more valuable problem is how a voice behaves inside a real conversation, including whether it earns trust over five minutes and holds up when a call gets messy. The company describes Chord as the latest expression of the core bet at Decagon Labs: that for customer interactions, a model fine-tuned for a specific task outperforms a general-purpose frontier model built for everything.

Jonas Reeve, Cognitive AI & AGI, AI Research Agent Jonas Reeve is an AI-generated analyst at Unite.AI, focusing on cognitive AI, artificial general intelligence (AGI), and the theoretical foundations of machine intelligence. His work explores how learning, reasoning, memory, and abstraction emerge in both biological and artificial systems, drawing connections between modern AI architectures and long-standing questions in cognitive science and philosophy of mind. With a conceptual and reflective approach, Jonas examines frameworks such as reasoning models, agentic systems, emergent cognition, and alignment theory, aiming to clarify what progress toward AGI actually means—and what it does not. Rather than chasing timelines or hype, he emphasizes first principles, conceptual rigor, and the limits of current models. proofCandidates.title: Decagon Partners With Databricks on Data, Models and Marketplace
proofCandidates.summary: Decagon announced a September 30, 2026 partnership with Databricks enabling zero-copy data sharing and model serving via Unity Gateway. The deal includes Decagon's AI agents accessing governed customer data and availability on Databricks Marketplace, with insights flowing back to enrich business tables.
proofCandidates.fullText:
Decagon announced a partnership with Databricks on September 30, 2026 that pairs zero-copy data sharing between the two platforms with Databricks-based model serving and planned availability of its customer-facing AI agents on Databricks Marketplace. The announcement on Decagon’s blog was co-authored by Roger Liang, Decagon’s Strategic Alliances & Partnerships Lead, and Mohsen Malik, Head of Applications Partnerships at Databricks. It describes the Databricks Data + AI Platform as a unified, governed foundation for enterprise data and AI that holds the full record of every customer, including orders, payments, entitlements, and product usage. “Through this partnership, Decagon agents can access governed data from Databricks when they need it, while insights from those conversations can flow back into Databricks and become useful across the rest of the business,” said Reynold Xin, Cofounder & Chief Architect at Databricks. “We’re excited to work with the Decagon team to make enterprise customer agents more context aware while keeping data governance at the center.” Zero-Copy Data in Both Directions Decagon said its user memory captures a customer’s context and preferences across conversations, while the Databricks platform holds what customers did: every order and payment, the products they actually use, and the scores a data team computed from all of it. Joining the two has typically meant building bespoke data pipelines that data engineers own indefinitely, with a copy of sensitive customer data landing somewhere new. In regulated industries, that copy is what holds up approval, because security teams ask where customer data goes, who can see it, and what happens to it afterward. With zero-copy OpenSharing governed by Unity Catalog, agents read the customer record directly from Databricks the moment they need it, with no ETL required, under permissions the customer’s team sets. Data also flows back. Every Decagon conversation can be pushed to the Databricks platform as structured data, including intent tags, root-cause attribution, escalation drivers, and user sentiment. Decagon says these insights enrich revenue, retention, and product tables and feed Duet Autopilot, so richer context produces better-validated agent updates. Decagon introduced user memory in a March 9, 2026 product post. The feature is built on a user-level abstraction that builds across interactions, storing conversational history and extracting structured signals such as feature requests, sentiment, and stated preferences attached to each customer’s profile. Storage is opt-in, with expiration and redaction controls, audit logs, and full data portability, according to the company. Model Serving Through Unity Gateway Decagon said it has added Databricks as a model serving provider and will soon join the Built-On program, giving two reasons. Its core constellation of models is post-trained for customer experience and carries the majority of the company’s traffic. For everything else, Unity Gateway provides day-zero access to popular state-of-the-art open-source and frontier models without a separate integration for each provider, model choice that Decagon says helps it avoid lock-in as the AI ecosystem evolves. The second reason, according to Decagon, is governance. Every turn in a conversation sends a request to a model, raising questions about which provider handled it, what the prompt contained, and whether any of it was retained. Most agent platforms log that activity themselves, in a separate console with retention terms they set, leaving one more system for a customer’s security team to review and trust. Routing through Unity Gateway means Unity Catalog’s permissions, lineage, and audit trails cover that inference activity, so the security team sees Decagon’s guardrails and its own governance in one place. Procurement Through Databricks Marketplace Decagon is listed as a launch partner on Databricks Marketplace, a virtual storefront for purchasing select partner products. Customers will be able to use their existing vendor relationship with Databricks to simplify billing and procurement when purchasing Decagon, and the company says the arrangement will help customers take weeks off the agent deployment path. Databricks opened the storefront on June 15, 2026, bringing third-party applications to Databricks Marketplace with more than 20 launch partners and introducing Marketplace Commit Drawdown, which lets customers acquire third-party data and AI solutions using existing Databricks universal commits. In the same announcement, Databricks said Delta Sharing had evolved into OpenSharing, a Linux Foundation project it described as the first open, vendor-neutral protocol for securely sharing AI assets, including Agent Skills, AI models, and unstructured data. Decagon will be available through the Databricks Marketplace, and the company is directing existing Databricks customers to book a demo.

proofCandidates.title: Plaid teams with decagon on conversational AI
proofCandidates.summary: Plaid and Decagon announced a partnership to let agents securely connect bank accounts within conversations, enabling actions like fraud resolution and claim processing. The partnership allows agents to resume multi-day tasks with persistent account access and maintains security guardrails and compliance.
proofCandidates.fullText:
Decagon and Plaid are announcing a partnership. With Plaid, customers can now securely connect their bank accounts within a Decagon conversation and take action on bank connections, failed payments, and disputed charges.
Financial services is one of our fastest-growing verticals, with agents in production at Square, Affirm, Chime, Valon, and more. Many of the most common requests in financial services require customers to log into their bank accounts first. That meant sending them outside the conversation to authenticate their account, which breaks the conversation and often ends it.
Working with Plaid, your agent can now:
Finish what the conversation started. Resolve account issues in real-time, without sending the consumer outside an agent conversation.
Pick up financial tasks that span days or weeks. Resume a claim, application, or dispute with full context, including the steps that need bank access.
Extend the same trust to work within user accounts. Permission, guardrails, and review stay exactly as you already run them.
“Across Plaid's AI customers, thousands of consumers are linking billions of dollars in accounts to AI platforms every single day to help navigate their finances. Our partnership with Decagon helps us enable our customers to meet the growing demand for more contextualized financial support.” - Kathleen McGuirk, Head of AI GTM at Plaid
Finish what the conversation started
Some of the highest-volume intents in financial services workflows are the ones that require the user to authenticate and login to their account.
Now, your agent can prompt users to connect their accounts through Plaid Link once, which enables secure, permissioned access to their financial data. Within the Decagon chat interface, the agent has the potential to manage fraud resolution, process an insurance claim, and even move a loan application past verification, alongside other long-term tasks.
Pick up work that spans days or weeks
Most financial services work unfolds over days or weeks: an insurance claim is filed today and settles three weeks out or a payment fails on the 3rd and has to be recovered before the 15th of the month. Both of these situations commonly require a handful of separate touchpoints between a business and a customer.
Your agent already carries context across sessions and channels, so it knows what has been collected and what is still outstanding. When your systems signal that the next step is ready, the agent picks it up and continues from there. Because the account connection from the first conversation persists, the agent can act on that step without starting over from authentication.
Extend the same trust to work within user accounts
An agent that can act on a customer’s account requires the highest bar for security and oversight.
That starts with permission. The customer grants access through Plaid, and the agent asks only for what the workflow needs like account details and a balance lookup. Credentials go directly to the bank, and customers can review every connection they’ve made and disconnect any of them in Plaid’s portal.
Guardrails within the Decagon platform run before, during, and after every conversation, and Watchtower, our always-on monitoring and QA, scores 100% of conversations in real time against your team’s criteria. Because agent logic is written in natural language with Agent Operating Procedures (AOPs), compliance teams can read and approve the procedures the agent follows and trace any conversation step by step, so regulated teams can audit any decision the moment they need to. Decagon is SOC-2 Type 2, GDPR, CCPA, and PCI compliant.

proofCandidates.title: Decagon vs Sierra: Real Cost and Resolution Pricing Compared (2026)
proofCandidates.summary: Decagon and Sierra both bill per resolved conversation, while Retell AI offers transparent per-minute pricing. Sierra raised $950 million in May 2026 at a $15.8 billion valuation, while Decagon raised $250 million in January 2026. Retell AI is recommended for teams needing same-day voice deployment, while Sierra suits Fortune 500 buyers with six-figure budgets.
proofCandidates.fullText:
Decagon and Sierra both bill per resolved conversation rather than per minute, and neither publishes a rate card. That single shared decision drives most of the difference between them, and most of the surprise in year two. Here is what each one actually costs, how each defines a resolution, and when a per-minute platform is the better fit. At first glance, Sierra and Decagon look like siblings. They are not the same size any more. Sierra raised $950 million in May 2026 at a $15.8 billion post-money valuation led by Tiger Global and GV, on a reported $150 million of ARR. Decagon raised a $250 million Series D in January 2026 led by Coatue and Index Ventures, tripling its valuation to $4.5 billion. Both sell to enterprise customer experience teams, and neither publishes a public price. Pick the wrong one and you are not out a few hundred dollars in trial credits. You are out a six-figure annual commitment, three to six months of procurement, and a forward-deployed engineer's calendar. This comparison is not another feature grid. We modeled the real annual cost at pilot, mid-market, and enterprise tiers, compared voice latency against what each vendor claims, and pulled direct user sentiment from G2 and public reviews. We also included Retell AI as a third reference point. Retell is a Customer Experience AI Platform where voice is the entry channel rather than the whole product, and it sits in a different commercial category: transparent per-minute pricing, self-serve signup, and an in-house command centre instead of a six-month implementation. Teams that need phone volume handled this quarter, and that want to own the configuration rather than hand it to a forward-deployed engineer, should have it on the shortlist from the start. voice automation with transparent per-minute pricing, it is the name that keeps surfacing in the follow-up research. Quick Answer: Who Should Pick What Retell AI is the best fit for most teams that do real call volume. Retell prices voice in a published range of $0.07 to $0.31 per minute depending on the model, voice and add-ons you choose, with no platform fee and no annual minimum. HIPAA ships on standard plans with a self-signable BAA. Build the agent you actually want, then price that configuration on the pricing page, because the floor and the ceiling differ by more than 4x. Retell AI runs production voice for enterprise and mid-market teams across healthcare, insurance, logistics and retail. Around 80% of production minutes run through agents customers built and manage themselves, and you can be live in a day without a procurement cycle. Sierra is the right call only if you are a Fortune 500 buyer with a $200K to $350K year-one budget, multi-channel digital CX at the center of your brand, and the patience for a forward-deployed-engineer engagement. Sierra wins on brand tone, governance and enterprise reach. It states it works with 40 percent of the Fortune 50, and names ADT, Chime, Cigna, Nordstrom, Nubank, Ramp, Rocket Mortgage, SiriusXM, Singtel and Wayfair among its customers. Decagon works best if your support volume sits mostly in chat and email, you have engineers to build and tune Agent Operating Procedures, and you are comfortable with per-conversation or per-resolution billing starting around $50K platform fee plus usage. Voice is newer than the chat and email backbone, but it is no longer an afterthought. Decagon Voice launched in 2025, Voice 2.0 reached general availability in September 2025 with outbound calling and cross-channel memory, and the March 2026 Proactive Agents launch added outbound voice with branded caller IDs, voicemail detection, redial cadences and Missions for campaign management. Now the details. 1. Setup and Time to First Live Call This matters because enterprise AI contracts routinely stall in month three of a six-month rollout, and the platform that ships sooner earns the renewal. Sierra ships a managed implementation, not software. Sierra operates closer to a consulting engagement than a SaaS product. Forward-deployed engineers work alongside your team to connect CRMs, knowledge bases, order systems, and data warehouses, and to build out the agent logic in the Agent SDK while your CX team adjusts tone in Agent Studio. Sierra publishes no pricing, and sierra.ai/pricing returned a 404 when checked in September 2026. Third-party buyer guides consistently model a year-one budget of $200,000 to $350,000, with a platform commitment reported from about $150,000 and one-time implementation of $50,000 to $200,000. Sierra has never confirmed any of those numbers, so treat them as market estimates rather than list prices. The timeline moved in 2026. Sierra shipped Ghostwriter in March 2026, an agent that builds agents from uploaded SOPs, transcripts and plain English, explicitly aimed at reducing the forward-deployed engineering work that used to define a Sierra rollout. Third-party guides now put typical onboarding at 4 to 10 weeks, stretching to several months for complex regulated deployments. Assume weeks, not days, and assume a sales cycle in front of it. Decagon is faster, but still engineering-led. Decagon's Agent Operating Procedures let non-technical operators define workflows in plain English, which compresses the iteration loop once engineers have done the initial integration work. In 2026 Decagon added Duet, an AI partner that drafts and refines AOPs from real transcripts, generates test scenarios and runs root cause analysis on low-scoring conversations, plus Agent Workbench for debugging. Decagon later shipped Duet Autopilot for automatic self-improvement. If you last evaluated Decagon in 2025, the build experience has changed materially. G2 reviewers report some deployments going live in under a week for simple use cases. That said, the platform still requires engineers to handle CRM and data integrations, set up guardrails, and connect voice telephony. A $50K-ish platform fee plus per-conversation or per-resolution usage kicks in on day one regardless of pilot outcomes. Retell ships same day for most teams. You sign up with $10 in free credits, pick a template for receptionists, outbound sales, or lead qualification, adjust the prompt, attach a phone number, and test in the dashboard within an hour. There is no sales call, no SOW, no forward-deployed engineer. The no-code builder and the developer SDK sit in the same product, so a solo operator can prototype on Monday and an engineer can harden it with custom functions on Tuesday. Teams running customer support pilots typically have 20 test calls logged by end of day one. Who this matters for: Solo founders and mid-market ops teams. Enterprise buyers with a dedicated implementation budget care less about setup speed and more about governance. Category winner: Retell AI because shipping same-day is a structural advantage Sierra and Decagon cannot match at their price point. 2. Voice Quality and Latency On inbound phone calls, latency above 800ms creates what reviewers call the "Zoom moment" where the caller thinks the line dropped and either repeats themselves or hangs up. Sierra added voice in 2024 as an extension of its digital platform. Sierra Voice AI handles inbound phone calls with a modular voice architecture that selects different model combinations per locale. Quality in English is reviewer-rated as natural for branded consumer experiences, with Casper's VP of Operations describing 24/7 multilingual coverage as a meaningful unlock. Sierra does not publish latency benchmarks, and no independent benchmark compares these platforms directly. What Sierra does publish is volume: it launched voice in October 2024 and reports handling more phone calls than chats within a year, across hundreds of millions of conversations. Judge the voice quality on your own test calls, not on either vendor's adjectives. Sierra launched voice in October 2024 and reported a year later that voice had overtaken chat as its primary channel. In August 2026 it shipped Voice Personas, which lets an agent adjust pacing, respond to interruptions and switch voice or language mid-call, powered by a constellation of voice models chosen per persona and locale. Sierra is a genuine voice competitor now, not a chat platform with a phone bolt-on. The real difference is the commercial model and who can get their hands on it. Decagon Voice 2.0 claims sub-second latency. Decagon launched Voice 2.0 with interruption handling, custom tone controls, and branded caller IDs, and added proactive outbound voice in spring 2026. Integrations run through Amazon Connect, RingCentral, and SIP trunking. The platform is new enough that independent latency benchmarks are scarce, and G2 reviewers note that voice capabilities are "still evolving" compared to the chat and email backbone. For companies whose support volume is primarily text, voice is a useful add-on; for phone-first operations, it is not yet the first-principles offering. Retell is voice-first by design. The orchestration stack is proprietary rather than stitched from public APIs, which is why latency stays consistent under load rather than drifting during concurrency spikes. Voice providers include ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Cartesia, and PlayHT with automatic fallback if a vendor has an outage. Platform Claimed latency Measured range Worst case reported Sierra Not published Unbenchmarked Reviewer-flagged as variable Decagon Sub-second (Voice 2.0) Limited public benchmarks Unknown Retell AI Not published Not published Not published Who this matters for: Any team where inbound phone is the primary channel. Sierra and Decagon's voice layers are credible for brands that do mixed-channel CX. For voice-first deployments like healthcare scheduling, insurance intake, or EV support, Retell's measured consistency is the relevant number. Category winner: Retell AI because proprietary turn-taking on a purpose-built voice stack holds under load. 3. Real Annual Cost at Pilot, Mid-Market, and Enterprise Tiers Sierra and Decagon do not bill per minute, so apples-to-apples with Retell requires modeling annual cost across three realistic deployment scales. Assumptions: a mid-complexity support agent handling a mix of FAQs and multi-step workflows, one channel at pilot, two to three channels at mid-market, full omnichannel at enterprise. That sounds risk free until you succeed: the better your agent gets, the more you pay, and the definition of a resolution is a commercial negotiation rather than a technical fact. Decagon makes the same point about its own category, noting that most of its customers choose per-conversation pricing precisely to avoid arguing over what counts as resolved. Per-minute pricing has the opposite shape. Your unit cost does not climb because the agent got good, and a finance team can model it in a spreadsheet before signing. Run a low-cost pilot first and let the volume data, not a resolution definition, set the contract. Retell at 50K interactions still costs a fraction of either, with transparent pricing that a finance team can model in a spreadsheet. The hidden costs worth naming: Sierra's "outcome" definitions are negotiated and can trigger billing even when an agent transfers to a human, Decagon's per-conversation model exposes you to volume spikes during Black Friday or product launches, and both require professional services line items that are easy to underestimate in procurement. Enterprise buyers with dedicated CX budgets and outcome-based ROI models should include all three. Category winner: Retell AI because the per-minute model is the only one in the three that a finance team can forecast without a custom contract. 4. Conversation Design and Flexibility Sierra splits developers and operators across two interfaces. The Agent SDK is where engineers write composable skills, connect to CRMs and APIs, and define version-controlled workflows. The Agent Studio is where the CX team adjusts tone, runs multivariate tests, and labels training data. Sierra closed most of this gap in late 2025. Agent Studio 2.0 hands CX and ops teams the same building blocks engineers use in the Agent SDK, and teams can now configure integrations from a library without code. The remaining dependency is commercial rather than technical: you reach those tools through an enterprise contract and an implementation engagement, not a signup form. Reviewers consistently describe Sierra deployments as deeply customizable but deeply dependent on the forward-deployed engineering relationship. Decagon's AOPs are the strongest natural-language workflow system in the category. Agent Operating Procedures let a non-technical support manager write "if a customer asks for a refund over $100, verify their purchase date and escalate to billing," and the AI compiles that into enforceable logic. AOPs are the capability Decagon leads with, and Decagon has doubled down on them: Duet, launched in March 2026, is itself built on AOPs and generates, tests and refines them automatically. The caveat buyers report is that writing good AOPs is real work. Complex operations with undocumented logic can spend months getting them right, which is the opposite of the plain-English promise. The tradeoff is that AOPs still need engineers for the initial integration work, guardrail setup, and the observability layer (Watchtower). Complex workflows also run into the "single-agent mindset" problem where every use case lives in one giant agent, making staged rollouts harder. Retell runs a drag-and-drop conversational flow builder on top of full developer access. Warm call transfer with full conversation context, real-time calendar sync to book appointments, and a knowledge base that auto-syncs from your website are all built in rather than bolted on as add-ons. All three platforms now ship simulation testing. Sierra runs Simulations in both the Agent SDK and Agent Studio, and tests Voice Personas against thousands of simulated interactions before deployment. Decagon ships Simulations as part of the Duet stack alongside versioning and Watchtower. The difference is access, not existence: Retell's simulation suite sits behind a self-serve signup, while Sierra's and Decagon's sit behind an enterprise contract. That single feature catches enough production regressions to justify the platform on its own for any team iterating on prompts weekly. Retell has the broadest plug-and-play integration directory of the three. Anything else connects over elastic SIP trunking, custom functions or webhooks, so bring-your-own-carrier deployments work without a services engagement. Deployment options include native Twilio, SIP for bring-your-own-carrier, and a web SDK for browser-based voice that requires no telephony at all. Developers get custom functions, webhooks, and a real-time function-calling API that the other two platforms treat as enterprise features. Who this matters for: Teams running modern SaaS stacks (HubSpot, Shopify, Slack, Notion) get plug-and-play coverage from Retell that Sierra requires a forward-deployed engineer to replicate. Teams embedded in Zendesk benefit from Decagon. Teams with legacy contact centers (Avaya, Genesys) can use all three but will pay implementation fees on Sierra and Decagon that Retell avoids. Category winner: Retell AI for breadth and self-serve setup, Decagon a close second for CRM and helpdesk depth. 6. Compliance, Security, and Support Sierra is built for regulated enterprise from day one. SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, HIPAA, and GDPR certifications are all standard, with strict PII redaction, audit trails, and encryption designed for banks, healthcare, and regulated consumer brands. The Constellation architecture routes across multiple LLM providers with guardrails to reduce hallucination risk. Support is white-glove: dedicated customer success, ongoing optimization, and forward-deployed engineers. The cost of that service is embedded in the six-figure contract, which means smaller teams cannot access it at any price. Decagon ships enterprise-grade compliance with usage-based access. SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, and HIPAA are all supported. Watchtower provides real-time QA and guardrails, and AOPs make compliance logic auditable in plain English. Support is strong for enterprise customers (dedicated Agent Product Managers and Forward-Deployed Engineers), but lighter for smaller deployments. The platform's relative newness means fewer long-term enterprise case studies than Sierra has accumulated. Retell includes HIPAA on standard plans with a self-service BAA portal. If you work in healthcare, financial services, or insurance, you can sign a BAA in the dashboard without procurement involvement. Pine Park Health, a senior care provider using Retell for patient scheduling, reported a 38% increase in scheduling NPS while freeing their clinical team from phone tag. Sierra wins on deepest enterprise governance, Decagon matches on certifications, and Retell wins on accessibility because the self-service BAA removes a two-week legal back-and-forth. Category winner: Retell AI on practical compliance accessibility, Sierra on depth of governance for Fortune 500 deployments. 7. Real User Sentiment (From G2, Reddit, Product Hunt) Rather than summarize, here is what actual users say about each platform. Sierra: "Sierra is the best tool to create AI agents for all kinds of platforms. The accuracy of the agents is very good. The implementation and integration have been like a cake walk." (G2) "User friendly interface, the software has a user-friendly interface that makes it easy for staff to navigate and perform tasks efficiently." (G2) "Reported bugs and rough edges compared to some more focused voice players." (Independent review, Vellum) Average sentiment: strongly positive among Fortune 500 buyers with deep pockets, mixed for teams outside that profile because of opaque pricing and consulting-engagement deployment model. Decagon: "The biggest upside of using Decagon isn't simply the assumption of repetitive day-to-day tasks that would normally be done manually, but that Decagon allows us to evaluate data on a much deeper level." (G2) "Decagon is still a new product, and lacks maturity in some of its features." (G2, balanced review) "Decagon solved our main problem of scaling customer support at cost. AI agents allow for near unlimited scalability in any language." (G2) Average sentiment: positive among mid-to-large tech companies (Duolingo, Notion, Rippling), with consistent caveats about platform newness, voice still evolving, and engineering resources required for deployment. (G2) "Lucas answers calls in seconds, handles urgent EV support at scale, cuts support costs by over 50%, and significantly improves our SaaS margins." Carter Li, CEO, SWTCH "Agents can sometimes include filler words or sound slightly robotic without careful prompt tuning." (G2, balanced review) Average sentiment: strongly positive, with the one recurring mild criticism being that prompts need tuning for full naturalness out of the box. Category winner: Retell AI on volume of positive voice-specific sentiment, with Decagon genuinely competitive on chat and email sentiment. Decision Framework If you are running inbound customer support where sub-800ms latency is non-negotiable and your ops team needs to iterate on scripts without a developer in the loop, Retell is the clearest fit. Sierra and Decagon can do voice, but neither treats it as the center of gravity the way a phone-first stack requires. If you are running high-volume outbound campaigns like appointment reminders, surveys, and lead follow-up, Retell handles most use cases cleanly because batch call functionality and outbound AI telemarketing are built into the core platform. Decagon's spring 2026 proactive outbound voice is worth piloting if you already run your chat and email on Decagon. If you are a Fortune 500 consumer brand where the AI agent's tone, governance, and cross-channel consistency are brand-critical (think Sonos, Casper, WeightWatchers), Sierra is the default. You are buying a managed service with a forward-deployed engineering team, and the $200K to $350K year-one budget is the price of that outcome. If you are in a regulated industry like healthcare, finance, or insurance, Retell's self-service HIPAA BAA and included compliance remove the pricing gotcha both competitors' deeper enterprise controls introduce. Matic Insurance handled 8,000+ calls on Retell in Q1 2025 with claims handle time dropping from 12.4 to 5.8 minutes. If you are an agency managing voice agents for multiple clients, Retell is the only platform where you can stand up a dedicated agent per client in minutes without a sales cycle. Sierra's engagement model and Decagon's enterprise minimums make multi-tenant deployment uneconomic at smaller client sizes. If you are a mid-market support team whose volume is mostly chat and email with some voice, Decagon's AOPs are genuinely the most powerful workflow engine in the category. The tradeoff is the $50K+ platform fee and enterprise sales cycle, which you are accepting for AOP-level control. The Bottom Line Sierra and Decagon are both legitimate platforms for the enterprise buyers they target. Sierra is the right answer for Fortune 500 consumer brands with deep CX budgets and a mandate to make the AI agent sound like the brand. Decagon is the right answer for tech companies doing primarily chat and email support who want natural-language workflow control and have engineers to back it up. Both teams have built real products with real customers, and both will continue to win deals in their respective niches. For most teams evaluating AI voice and customer experience platforms in 2026, Retell AI is the more balanced choice because it wins on the dimensions that matter most for production voice (measured latency, transparent pricing, same-day setup, HIPAA-ready) without forcing a six-figure commitment before you know whether the platform fits. The strongest test is to build the same basic agent on two platforms using free credits where available, run 20 real test calls, and see which one your team actually wants to keep using a week later.

proofCandidates.summary: Seven Decagon AI alternatives for customer support are compared, including Retell AI, Ada, Intercom Fin AI, Zendesk, Vapi AI, Freddy AI, and others. Decagon's platform fee is around $50,000 annually, while alternatives offer varying pricing and integration options.

Decagon AI is an AI platform designed for enterprise-level customer support automation. The idea is to create AI agents across channels that can think and solve problems like your best human agents. However, Decagon isn't the best fit for every business, especially for leaner teams or businesses seeking deeper task automation, flexible workflows, or faster deployment. As customer expectations evolve, businesses are realizing Decagon's standalone platform doesn't work well for them, especially if you're looking to improve your current setup, not tear it down and start over. We've put together a list of the 7 best alternatives and compared them across features, pricing, and user reviews. For each tool, we've called out what it does well and who should go for it, based on our testing. Let's get started. Why Look for Decagon Alternatives? The magic of Decagon is that it builds AI agents that do more than just read from a script. They learn from your past support conversations and can actually take action for customers across chat, email, and even voice calls. Still, many teams end up searching for Decagon alternatives for a few solid reasons: It is an expensive layer, not a replacement Decagon sits on top of the help desk you already run, so the six figures you spend on it are additive rather than a swap. The Model layer: Fin's specialised sub-models handle retrieval, ranking, summarisation, and escalation, helping agents recognise intent and detect sentiment in a way unseen in previous AI agents. Each layer in the Fin's architecture is optimized for accuracy and speed to deliver higher-quality answers across multiple brands, channels, and languages. Its no-code infrastructure lets you customise, test and improve agent performance without engineering or vendor involvement, and each piece of behaviour stays separately editable rather than bundled into one asset your team has to unpick. Intercom features: Personalise Fin to match your brand's tone, train it on your support knowledge and policies, and set how it handles complex tasks in over 45 languages.

Fin's content library makes it easy for your team to control, maintain and update all of the content Fin learns from in a centralized location.

Uses Custom Data Attributes (CDAs) when generating answers, allowing it to personalize responses based on what it already knows about a customer.

Fin Tasks allow you to automate more complex processes with Fin.

Fin can read and understand images, like screenshots, invoices, and error messages, so customers can share what they see without lengthy explanations. Fin AI integrations: Fin connects to the systems and channels you already use, through MCP or API Data Connectors. It supports integrations to every channel, from chat and email to voice. Fin AI pricing: Fin charges $0.99 per outcome when integrated with your current helpdesk, including Zendesk, Salesforce, HubSpot, and more. However, when using Intercom's helpdesk, you'll have to pay $0.99 per outcome +$29 per helpdesk seat per month. 4. Zendesk What does it do? Zendesk is a cloud-based customer service platform that helps businesses organize all their customer interactions in one sleek place. It includes a world-class ticketing system, robust live chat, a flexible help centre builder, and powerful reporting dashboards. Who is it for? Zendesk is incredibly versatile. While it works excellently for external customer support, many teams also use it internally for IT help desks or HR requests. Also, it works just as well for a small team as it does for a global enterprise. Zendesk AI is the intelligence layer built on top of Zendesk's established customer service platform. If you're already using Zendesk for messaging and ticketing, the AI feature integrates natively into your existing workflows. The platform focuses on three main areas: AI agents that can resolve customer issues autonomously

Copilot features that assist human agents with suggested replies and next steps

Administrative tools that help optimize operations Because Zendesk is so powerful and feature-rich, the platform offers an incredible amount of enterprise-grade functionality. Its tool is built for experts; it provides extensive opportunities for custom workflows, triggers, and automations. Zendesk's advantage is scale. If you're already using Zendesk, the AI features plug right into your existing setup. Conversation history stays unified. Agent handoff happens within the same workspace. Zendesk features: Zendesk's intelligent triage uses machine learning to look at incoming tickets and automatically sort, tag, and decide how important they are.

Suggest relevant responses that agents can use to handle common issues quickly.

Zendesk provides comprehensive reporting and analytics tools so you can keep track of how well its AI features are doing.

You can build structured conversation flows where the AI asks qualifying questions, collects information, and routes conversations based on the answers.

Zendesk offers an omnichannel experience that offers a single view of the entire customer journey. Zendesk AI integrations: The Zendesk Marketplace offers over 1000 integrations, making it easier to connect with tools you already use. Zendesk AI makes the most sense for teams already invested in the Zendesk ecosystem who want to add AI capabilities without switching platforms. Zendesk pricing: Zendesk offers transparent, tiered pricing: Plan Pricing AI Features Included Support Team $25/agent/month AI agents (Essential) Suite Team $69/agent/month AI agents, Generative replies, Knowledge Builder Suite Professional $149/agent/month Above + Copilot (5 uses/month), Up to 5 help centers Suite Enterprise $219/agent/month Above + Up to 300 help centers 5. Vapi AI What does it do? Vapi AI is a voice AI platform designed for teams who want to build AI voice agents from scratch. Who is it for? If you already have a tech stack that you use to run AI voice agents, then Vapi AI can be a good choice. Businesses with limited technical bandwidth might struggle to maintain it due to multiple configurations. Vapi AI is a developer-centric AI voice assistant platform that allows you to create, test and deploy voice assistants into web or mobile apps, CRMs, or customer service systems. You get to choose the speech-to-text, a large language model, and text-to-speech, and Vapi handles the call. While Vapi AI offers built-in tools for the most common use cases, like booking appointments or sending messages, you can extend the capabilities for your agent by connecting it to external APIs, databases, or business logic. This way, you can: Control how the agent listens, thinks, and responds on each call.

Connect those agents to your existing tools and internal APIs.

Create custom voice agents for support, sales, or operations. Custom tools go beyond simple conversions and provide systems with up-to-date insights that are outside their LLM's knowledge repository, like raising an invoice or looking up a customer's status in CRM. While this may seem like a dream setup, businesses with limited tech bandwidth often struggle to maintain it; besides, they have to bear the cost of the speech-to-text, LLM, and voice model, along with Vapi's premium pricing. Vapi AI features: Vapi AI is super flexible; you can mix and match models for different stages of the conversational flow. It supports a wide range of providers across different components including, LLM providers, voice providers, transcription and SIP providers.

Vapi AI Flow Studio is a visual, no-code, drag-and-drop visual flow builder that maps out the basic conversations of your AI agent.

Supports over 100 languages for voice input and output.

Generates summaries and structured call data that can be pushed into CRMs or ticketing systems. The analysis system covers key events, basic sentiment and outcome scoring.

Upload PDFs or text documents so the agent has reference material during calls. Vapi AI Integrations Vapi AI offers limited pre-built integrations, however you can seamlessly connect with GoHighLevel, Make, Google Calendar, Google Sheet and Slack. For other integrations, you can create custom webhooks to be accessed via calls. Vapi AI Pricing Vapi's hosting cost starts at $0.05 per minute, but it's actually a fraction of the total deployment cost. The true meaning of "bring your own stack" means that you've paid for all the providers, including Vapi's hosting fee, to run your AI voice agent efficiently. When you add this up, the actual cost comes around $0.13 - $0.31+ Besides, businesses choosing "pay-as-you-go" pricing have to pay $1,000 per month add-on for HIPAA compliance. 6. Freddy AI What does it do? Freddy AI is an AI layer that's built into the Freshworks ecosystem, designed to help the customer support team rather than replace them. Who is it for? Freddy AI is best for teams already committed to Freshworks. The deep integration with Freshdesk, Freshsales and Freshservice means seamless data flow and unified reporting. Freshdesk is a mature customer support platform that has been around since 2010 and serves over 74,000 businesses worldwide. Freddy AI is the AI layer that adds automation and intelligence to the existing Freshdesk platform. It operates on a simple premise: connecting your existing Freshworks account, enabling the features you want and letting the system learn from your data. Freshworks positions it as "People-first AI" that works alongside your team. It comes with three core components: Freddy AI Agent manages customer conversations across email, chat, WhatsApp, and social channels.

Freddy AI Copilot supports agents by drafting responses, summarising tickets, and analyzing customer sentiment.

Freddy AI Insights delivers analytics and reports that help teams identify trends and optimize operations. For the AI agent component, you get access to pre-built "Vertical AI Agents" that come with 50+ agentic workflows for common scenarios. This includes order tracking, subscription changes, refund processing and appointment scheduling. The agents integrate directly with Shopify, Stripe, PayPal, FedEx, and other tools to take real actions, not just provide answers. Freddy AI can handle conversations consistently across email, webchat, WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger, and Instagram without dropping context. It also supports over 60+ languages, making it accessible for global support operations. Freshdesk features: Freddy can handle tasks within chats, streamlining operations like order checks or bookings.

Operates across multiple messaging channels, ensuring support is accessible wherever customers are.

Directs inquiries to the appropriate teams or agents, optimizing response times and accuracy.

Freddy Copilot centralizes customer interactions for tailored service suggestions and quick issue resolutions. Freshdesk integrations: Freddy AI integrates with over 1,200 enterprise apps across industry verticals. You can also access pre-built connectors that connect Freshworks' suite of products to any API-enabled system, be it cloud or legacy on-prem applications. Freshdesk pricing: To access Freddy AI features, you'll want to be on one of Freshworks' professional-tier plans: Pro Plan: $49 per agent, per month (when billed annually).

$49 per agent, per month (when billed annually). Enterprise Plan: $79 per agent, per month (when billed annually). These plans are excellent for established teams, and both come with an initial 500 sessions with the AI Agent for free. 7. Bland AI What does it do? Bland AI offers an easy-to-integrate API infrastructure that makes sending an AI phone call simple. It can handle thousands of calls a day, all from your own dedicated GPUs. Who is it for? Bland AI is trusted for its scalability, making it ideal for organizations that handle high call volumes like healthcare, logistics, and fintech. It's primarily designed for enterprises and developer-heavy teams that want extreme flexibility and deep integration. Bland AI focuses exclusively on voice and SMS automation for enterprises. It offers an in-built easy-to-integrate voice call API that makes sending an AI phone call simple (just requiring ten lines of code). Rather than hand-holding your team into creating voice agents, it provides raw building blocks like webhooks, memory stores, pathways and voice cloning, so you can craft a unique voice agent build for your business needs. In short, Bland AI can: Handle thousands of calls a day, all from your own dedicated GPUs.

Integrate with your CRM, ERP, and anywhere else.

Clone any voice from a single short MP3 or audio clip, no fine-tuning required.

Analyze every call with insights like sentiment analysis and call scoring.

Extend AI agents across channels, including calls, SMS and chats. Besides integration with your favourite tools, Bland AI allows you to create custom tools and fine-tune mid-call sessions using APIs, leading to lower latency and contextual answers. However, without technical knowledge, it would be difficult to create custom tools and integrate them with your voice bot. You can utilize some of its pre-made templates, but if you want to customize your voice agent, you'll need to work with Bland's staff. Bland AI features: Bland's "Conversational Pathways" maps out a conversation by splitting prompts into unique nodes, helping your voice agents make decisions.

Through APIs and integrations, the agent can pull information, update records, and trigger workflows instantly, turning it from a talking bot into a fully capable operational assistant.

Bland AI has a collection of high-quality, pre-recorded human voices varying across language, accent, and gender.

For conversations to feel personal, Bland AI has a new "AI memory" feature that enables agents to recall information from past interactions. Bland AI integrations Bland AI offers live integration with Salesforce CRM, Cal.com & Calendly, Notion, Twilio and native SMS integration. Bland AI Pricing: Bland AI offers a simple usage-based pricing per $0.09 / min inbound and outbound voice calls. This is your baseline cost for any connected call lasting more than a few seconds. There are different costs subject to a $0.015 minimum cost each attempt, call transfers ($0.025 per minute) and voicemails ($0.09 / min). Choosing the right Decagon alternative for your organization Choosing the right Decagon alternative depends on how you currently run support, how much control you want over automation, and whether you're optimizing for speed, flexibility, or deep customization. Some tools act as full AI agents that handle conversations end-to-end, while others layer intelligence on top of your existing systems. Here's how to think about it: If you want a voice-first AI agent that can handle conversations and actions end-to-end, Retell AI is the strongest fit. It's built for teams that want to automate inbound and outbound calls, manage multi-turn conversations, and trigger real-time workflows (like bookings or CRM updates) without heavy engineering. It works especially well if voice is a core support or sales channel. If your priority is adding AI on top of your existing helpdesk (without replacing it), Ada and Intercom Fin AI are better choices. Ada is ideal for enterprise teams that want structured automation, strong analytics, and multi-channel orchestration. Fin AI, on the other hand, offers more flexibility and no-code control, making it easier for teams to customize behavior, tone, and workflows without relying on engineers. If you're already deeply invested in a support ecosystem, Zendesk AI or Freddy AI (Freshworks) make the most sense. These tools integrate natively into their respective platforms, keeping your workflows, ticket history, and reporting unified. They're best for teams that want to enhance existing operations rather than introduce a new system. If you need maximum flexibility and are comfortable with a developer-heavy setup, Vapi AI and Bland AI are worth considering. These platforms give you full control over how your AI agents are built, from choosing models to designing logic and integrations. They're powerful, but they require technical resources to implement and maintain effectively. If your main concern is avoiding complexity and speeding up deployment, tools like Retell AI and Intercom Fin AI stand out again. They offer faster time-to-value with minimal setup, making them ideal for lean teams or companies that want to start seeing ROI quickly. Five questions worth asking before you sign These come up repeatedly once teams are past the demo. They apply to every platform on this page, including ours. Does the price change when call length or the model changes? Ask what your rate looks like at your actual average handle time, not the demo call.

Ask what your rate looks like at your actual average handle time, not the demo call. Can the agent create the case in your ticketing system, or only transfer? Transfer-only means a human still does the data entry.

Transfer-only means a human still does the data entry. Where does call data live, at rest and in transit? Some teams need processing to stay in a specific country, and that is a contract question, not a settings question.

Some teams need processing to stay in a specific country, and that is a contract question, not a settings question. Does recording continue after the call transfers to a human? This is where end-to-end evidence usually breaks.

This is where end-to-end evidence usually breaks. What happens to the rate when volume triples?Ask before you sign, because the renegotiation happens after you have already migrated. Wrapping Up All of these Decagon alternatives offer unique strengths that can transform your customer interaction, but which one should you choose? When evaluating vendors, prioritize: How well the AI handles real support conversations

Flexibility beyond a single-agent setup

Integration depth with your existing tech stack

Ease of setup without heavy engineering

Transparency and control over AI behavior

Total cost of ownership, not just license fees Considering these factors, Retell AI is the voice-first pick: low-latency infrastructure you can point at your own carrier, published pricing with no platform fee, and a deployment you can start today rather than after a procurement cycle. Prove it on your own calls before you sign anything. Run a pilot on the workflow you care most about, against your real volume, and compare the outcomes to what you have now. No enterprise agreement required to find out. Start your free trial with Retell today. FAQs 1. Why do businesses look for Decagon alternatives? Businesses often look for alternatives to Decagon AI because of its standalone setup that requires replacing existing tools like help desks, which adds friction for teams with established workflows. 2. Which Decagon alternatives support multi-agent orchestration and complex workflow handoffs? Platforms like Retell AI support more advanced orchestration by enabling structured workflows, modular logic, and task-based automation. This allows multiple specialized flows or agents to handle different parts of a conversation, making them better suited for complex support environments. 3. Which Decagon alternatives support voice and chat from the same platform? Decagon, Retell AI, Freddy AI and Bland AI all run voice and chat from one platform. The question worth asking is whether the voice side is built on the vendor's own telephony or resold, and whether you can point it at the carrier and dialer you already have. 4. How does pricing compare between Decagon and Retell AI? Decagon charges a platform fee of around $50,000 a year before a single conversation is handled, then per-conversation or per-resolution usage on top. Third-party contract data puts the median annual deal near $386,000. Retell charges no platform fee and no subscription: you pay per voice minute and per chat message, every plan opens the entire platform, and you can start at zero. 5. How does Retell AI handle human handoff compared to Decagon? Both platforms warm-transfer with context. Retell goes further down the stack: it can sit inside an existing CCaaS or dialer over SIP, so the transfer lands in the queue your agents already work in rather than in a second system they have to watch.
